articles.title: GPT-6.1 Sol
articles.content:
We’re introducingGPT-6.1 Sol, an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches GPT-6 Astra’s intelligence on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token prices. Cached input costs just$0.10 per million tokens—95% less than standard input pricing and 50% less than GPT-6 Sol’s cached input pricing—giving developers more room to build and run capable agents that reuse context across requests.

Our most intelligent model for the
best results.

Near-Astra intelligence for a fifth of the price.

Fast and efficient everyday work
at scale.

GPT-6.1 Sol offers a new balance of capability and cost for important everyday work. It delivers substantial improvements over GPT-6 Sol across complex professional tasks, from writing and debugging code to understanding documents and executing multi-step business workflows. On several of these evaluations, it approaches GPT-6 Astra’s performance at substantially lower cost.

OnDeepSWE v1.1, which evaluates complex software-engineering tasks in real codebases, GPT-6.1 Sol matches GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth of the cost, while eclipsing GPT-6 Sol’s best score by 6.4 percentage points at a lower reasoning effort and cost.

InDeepSWE 1.1⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents solve original, long-horizon software engineering tasks.

OnGDP.pdf, which measures how accurately models answer professional questions using complex PDF documents, including tables, charts, diagrams, and fine-print details, GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than Opus 5.5 with fallbacks at less than half the cost per task across the tested reasoning settings. It also approaches GPT-6 Astra’s state-of-the-art performance at roughly one-fifth the cost per task.

InGDP.pdf⁠(opens in a new window), models must answer real-world prompts about complex PDFs pulled from professional workflows in finance, healthcare, legal, and seven other professional domains.

OnAutomationBench, which measures whether agents correctly complete multi-step business workflows, GPT-6.1 Sol scores 2.2 percentage points above Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort, at roughly a third of the cost. That score is also up 4.8 percentage points from GPT-6 Sol at the same setting.

InAutomationBench 1.0.6⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents are tested on end-to-end workflows using 47 tools across sales, marketing, operations, support, finance, and HR. The datapoint for Claude Fable 5.1 understates its actual cost, as it omits the cost of fallbacks, which occurred on ~40% of tasks.

GPT-6.1 Sol also makes substantial progress on tasks that require interacting with computer applications. OnOSWorld 2.0’s offline set, which evaluates agents on demanding computer-use workflows, GPT-6.1 Sol outperforms GPT-6 Sol by seven percentage points at maximum reasoning effort at less than half the cost. It comes within 2.1 percentage points of Astra’s score at maximum reasoning effort at roughly one-seventh the cost per task.

InOSWorld 2.0⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents attempt long-horizon computer-use workflows spanning everyday and professional tasks. We report the partial reward on the offline set from the v2026.08.08 release.

OnTerminal-Bench Science 0.1, which evaluates scientific workflows including data analysis, simulation, and theorem proving, GPT-6.1 Sol more than doubles GPT-6 Sol’s score at maximum reasoning effort at less than half the cost per task. At maximum effort, GPT-6.1 Sol costs $5.47 per task on average, compared with $23.21 for Opus 5.5 and $23.80 for Astra, delivering substantial scientific capability at over 75% lower cost than either model.

GPT-6 Astra still achieves the highest score among the models tested at 68.1%, and should be used for the most difficult scientific research tasks.

InTerminal-Bench Science 0.1⁠(opens in a new window), agents complete scientific research workflows using code and terminal tools, including analyzing data, running simulations, and fitting models.

GPT-6.1 Sol also improves factual accuracy on difficult prompts. Its largest factuality improvement over GPT-6 Sol comes at low reasoning effort, where it reduces the share of responses containing a factual error from 11.4% to 7.7%—a reduction of approximately 32%. Across the tested reasoning settings, its error rate remains within 1.9 percentage points of GPT-6 Astra’s, at less than one-fifth the cost per task.

This evaluation measures the share of answers containing at least one factual error on de-identified conversations where users flagged an earlier model’s error. These deliberately difficult prompts are not representative of typical usage.

We evaluate factuality on de-identified ChatGPT conversations where users had flagged a factual error from a prior model. These error-inducing conversations are not representative of typical usage, where factual errors are more rare.

GPT-6.1 Sol shows substantial improvements over GPT-6 Sol in our alignment evaluations, bringing it closer to GPT-6 Astra.

GPT-6.1 Sol is more transparent about its limitations and more reliable at respecting user intent and safety constraints. In challenging evaluations, it shows lower failure rates than GPT-6 Sol on transparency about broken search tools, respecting explicit restrictions, and avoiding unauthorized outcomes during agentic tasks. We observed no attempts to bypass an automated safety reviewer, matching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol. Full details can be found in theGPT-6.1 Sol system card addendum⁠(opens in a new window).

The evaluations below deliberately test challenging situations and do not measure failure rates in typical use.

GPT-6.1 Sol is available starting today to all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. GPT-6.1 Sol is not yet available in Chat. Developers can also access it through the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-sol. Its standard API prices are $2 per million input tokens, $0.10 per million cached input tokens, and $10 per million output tokens. In the coming days, we’ll also offer GPT-6.1 SolUltrafast⁠, with up to 8x faster token generation compared to its standard speed in Codex.

Evaluations of GPT were performed in our research environment or via our API, which may provide slightly different output from production ChatGPT due to differences in the system prompts, tools available, efforts, etc. Evaluations of competitor models were taken from publicly available reports.

articles.content:
November 3, 2026

Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products. These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster.

Across these projects, engineers need to bring together mechanical designs, electronics, software, and manufacturing requirements using specialized tools. We’re teaching models to support that work, from preparing drawings and setting up simulations to coordinating changes across disciplines. Our goal is to give engineers more time to explore ideas and improve designs.

Over the past year, improved frontier model capabilities have helped our internal teams test new ideas and iterate faster, and we are seeing early evidence of these capabilities improving professional workflows in industry as well. We’re working with collaborators to understand where these capabilities can make the biggest difference and what needs to improve. If you’re an engineer, engineering firm, or software vendor involved in the design, simulation, manufacturing, or production of complex physical products, we’d love towork with youto shape this effort around the tools you use and the problems you need to solve.

We testedAstra’s state-of-the-art performance⁠in multimodal and computer use workflows by seeing if we can createa device without any direct human edits. To do this, we used GPT‑6 to define the functional requirements and design the enclosure, printed circuit board (PCB), and software integrations needed to create a device users can use to talk to Codex.

Aesthetics and design:Astra developed the look of the device, drawing on our recentWork Louder⁠(opens in a new window)collaboration and references from games and toys.

Mechanical design:Astra designed theenclosure⁠(opens in a new window)and the internal structures that hold the components in place.

Electrical design:Astra selected the electrical components and designed the printed circuit board (PCB), including component placement and connections, to fit within the enclosure.

UI/UX and software:Astra designed the user interface and generated the firmware and software integrations needed to connect the device to Codex.

Two team members designed this test device with Astra in under a week while working on it as a side project. A contract manufacturer built a small batch of prototypes in under a month.

Getting the device ready for manufacturing still required several rounds of review and iteration. Astra did not consistently account for the manufacturer’s production limits, tolerances, or details required for assembly. These gaps are helping us identify what future models need to do better.

OpenAI’s hardware and infrastructure teams use Codex and ChatGPT to create and revise computer-aided design (CAD) models, prepare manufacturing drawings, set up simulations, and review designs. This work spans robotics and compute infrastructure. Since February, model usage across our hardware teams, measured in tokens, has grown 23-fold.

We’re also measuring progress in newer models on tasks that combine coding with engineering knowledge. BenchCAD 2.0 tests whether models can reconstruct 3D parts and assemblies and identify connections in circuit boards. A newer internal model achieved an average score of 0.875, compared with 0.594 for GPT‑6 Astra at its highest reasoning setting. While the engineering lifecycle includes many other elements beyond design, we view improvements in capability here as early evidence of the ability of AI models to positively impact iteration speed for professional workflows.

We’re working with a small group of industry collaborators to test these capabilities on real engineering problems. Their engineers review model outputs for accuracy and practical use, helping us understand which tasks models can support today and what needs to be improved for safe and reliable use.

We’re expanding our collaboration withChip Ganassi Racing(CGR) to explore how OpenAI models can accelerate engineering and prototyping. Working with its R&D team, we’re testing workflows that turn 3D scans of existing parts into editable CAD models and 2D manufacturing drawings. This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

CGR engineers review the models and drawings for accuracy and manufacturability. Their feedback helps us identify where models can reduce manual work and where further improvements are needed.

We’re also announcing a new research collaboration with Mazda. Our research and Forward Deployed Engineering teams are working with Mazda’s aerodynamics and crash-safety engineers to explore how OpenAI models can help develop and evaluate new vehicle designs.

The work uses simulations of airflow and structural behavior to explore improvements in performance while accounting for styling and cost. We’ll share more progress and results in the coming months.

GPT‑6 Astra helps Mazda’s aerodynamics engineers explore ways to reduce vehicle drag by modeling new nose shapes, simulating airflow, and refining the most promising designs. Agreement for use has been obtained from Mazda Motor Corporation. Any republication or reuse elsewhere is strictly prohibited.

We have been working closely with industry partners and early adopters to push the bounds of what we can do with AI agents in hardware and manufacturing. These early results have shown exciting promise, and we’re now looking for collaborators to accelerate these capability improvements and ensure we deploy these safely into industry.

If you are interested in working with us to shape the training and development of our frontier models by identifying high-value use cases, software tooling, or future opportunities in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, electromechanical design, mechatronics, or a related field, please fill outthis formand we'll be in touch.

articles.title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve: Cryptographic Proofs That a Reply Came From Committed Weights
articles.content: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team has released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype for provable inference. FlashProve is a zkSNARK system from Anthropic that proves a reply came from a committed model. The proof reveals nothing about the model weights. On Llama 4 Maverick, a 400B mixture-of-experts model, it proves about 110 tokens/second on 1 H100. For developers, this targets a real gap: today you cannot check which model actually answered your API call. TL;DR Size: Proves a 400B MoE model (~17B active per token); context capped at 1,024 tokens per request. Runs on: Prover needs 1 H100 80 GB, 24 CPU cores and ~290 GB host RAM. Verifier runs on a CPU, no GPU. Performance: Orders of magnitude faster than prior open-source zkML systems on the same 400B model. Best: 110 tokens/second proving on 1 H100, with 18.78 MB proofs checked in 17 seconds. Worst: Proving costs ~70 to 95x the GPU time of plain vLLM inference. What problem does provable inference solve? A user querying a model cannot verify which model produced the response. A routing service could swap in a cheaper model. An attacker could tamper with the token stream. Judging from output quality alone is unreliable. Anthropic lists 4 use cases: Regulators could confirm hardware serves inference, supporting AI pacing rules. Labs could detect tampered inference servers. Users could verify text provenance. Regulators could enforce serving of approved models only. How does FlashProve work? FlashProve has a prover (the model provider) and a verifier (the user). It runs in 2 phases: Offline: The provider publishes a commitment, a short fingerprint binding one exact set of weights. This takes about 39 minutes and covers about 16 million requests. Online: For each request, the GPU produces a proof that the committed model produced those tokens. The proof system compiles an interactive oracle proof into a cryptographic proof using hash functions. Anthropic says this offers post-quantum security. It is the same family used by validity-proof L2 networks such as Starknet. Three engineering choices drive the speed. Prover work scales with the ~17B active parameters, not all 400B. Requests are proved in batches after the fact, like prefill. Weights stream from host memory, so a single 80 GB GPU suffices. How fast is it? Benchmarks Anthropic measured the public 4-bit Maverick weights on 1 H100 with 24 CPU cores. Per the repo performance guide: Batch of 24: 111.23 tokens/second, ~221 to 226 seconds per batch. Batch of 1: 17.41 tokens/second. Batch of 64: 123.31 tokens/second, flagged as unreliable on 80 GB cards. Proof size: 18.78 MB. Client downloads ~6.5 MB once per commitment. Verification: 17 seconds on 24 threads, 21 seconds on 1 thread. Against vLLM running FP8 Maverick on 8 H100s, proving costs about 72x the GPU time per batch. At vLLM’s highest tested load, the gap is about 94x. & How does FlashProve compare with other zkML systems? MetricsFlashProveAttestableVerInfDeepProvezkLLMModel provenLlama 4 Maverick (400B MoE)Gemma 4 31B (dense)Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE)GPT-2, Gemma 3LLaMA-2-13BThroughput~110 tok/s53 to 77 tok/s~0.02 tok/s (1,000 tokens in 14.3 h)~2.9 tok/s (GPT-2), ~1.4 tok/s (Gemma 3)Full inference in under 15 minHardware1 H100 + 24 CPU cores1 H1001 DGX Spark1 machine; 31 tok/s distributedGPU (CUDA)Proof size18.78 MB4.35 to 7.92 MiB93.6 GBNot disclosedUnder 200 kBVerify time17 s (24 threads)157 to 648 ms17.7 h (20 cores)1 to 3.7 sNot disclosedContext1,024 tokensUp to 16K tokens1,000 tokensNot disclosedNot disclosedCode / licenseOpen, Apache 2.0Not open sourceOpen, MITOpen source per LagrangePaper (CCS 2024) How is the security checked? Cryptographic code is brittle, so Anthropic formalized the protocol in Lean. It proves completeness, soundness and zero knowledge. The README states a cheating provider is caught except with probability about q/2^124 + 2^-101. FlashProve ships 2 verifiers. A fast C++ verifier is for daily use but carries no formal guarantee. A slower Lean verifier is proven to accept only what the soundness theorem accepts. Anthropic team notes Claude helped optimize the system. Key Takeaways FlashProve proves a 400B MoE model at ~110 tokens/second on 1 H100. Proofs are 18.78 MB and verify on a CPU in 17 seconds. Proving costs ~70 to 95x the GPU time of vLLM inference. Security properties are formalized in Lean; weights stay hidden. Limited to 1,024 tokens, greedy decoding, and MoE models for now. Check out the research post, technical report, protocol specification and GitHub repo. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter. Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. articles.summary: 보도에 따르면 Anthropic은 응답이 사전에 확약된 모델 가중치에서 생성됐음을 증명하는 오픈소스 연구 프로토타입 FlashProve를 공개했다. zkSNARK를 이용해 가중치를 공개하지 않고 추론의 출처를 검증하며, 4,000억 매개변수 MoE 모델인 Llama 4 Maverick에서 H100 한 대로 초당 약 110토큰의 증명 처리 성능을 보고했다. 모델 제공자의 임의 교체나 추론 서버 변조를 확인할 수 있다는 점에서 API 신뢰성과 규제 검증에 의미가 있다. 다만 요청당 컨텍스트가 1,024토큰으로 제한되고 증명에 일반 vLLM 추론 대비 약 70~95배의 GPU 시간이 필요해 상용 적용에는 비용 장벽이 크다.

We’re raising rewards in OpenAI’s Security Bug Bounty program to further encourage independent researchers to pursue vulnerabilities in OpenAI software that our testing may have missed. We’re also introducing new incentives for researchers to earn more for higher quality vulnerability reports.

Independent security researchers play an essential role in protecting technology across the industry. At OpenAI, incentivizing responsible disclosure is a core part of our security model, complementing ourDefense Factory⁠work, where our engineers use our models to find weaknesses, reproduce them, and test fixes.

Today’s updates are designed to encourage and empower researchers, and to continue building a collaborative, community-first security environment.

We’re more than quadrupling the midpoint of our reward ranges for medium, high, and critical findings on average. A critical vulnerability in a core product such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform will now earn up to $30,000. Exceptional critical findings on those targets remain eligible for up to $100,000, and now up to $172,000 with bonuses. The full details are available inour security bug bounty program⁠(opens in a new window).

High-quality reports will be eligible to earn a bonus multiplier on the base bounty. A reliable proof of concept that isolates the bug, shows when it can be exploited, and demonstrates its impact gives us a head start on a fix. The quality multiplier recognizes the extra work that makes a finding especially useful.

To build long-term relationships and continuously empower our security community, we are introducing a tiered loyalty bonus program. This 5-tier system provides scaling bonuses to recognize, support, and celebrate researchers who consistently partner with us in making AI technology safer for everyone.

To support community engagement as technology evolves, priority campaigns will feature dedicated bonus pools for newly launched features. These short-term campaigns give researchers early, high-reward opportunities to test new developments and be recognized for their early contributions.

articles.title: 탈취한 AI 계정으로 하루 10만달러 ‘요금 폭탄’…구글, LLM재킹 공격 확산 경고
articles.content:
기업의 인공지능(AI) 모델 접근 권한을 탈취해 대규모 사용 요금을 발생시키고, 훔친 AI 서비스를 암시장에서 재판매하는 사이버 범죄가 확산하고 있다. 공격자들은 탈취한 API 키와 클라우드 계정을 이용해 고성능 AI 모델을 무단으로 호출하고, 사용 비용을 피해 기업에 떠넘기는 방식으로 수익을 창출하고 있다.

특히 하루 만에 10만달러 이상의 부정 사용 요금이 발생하거나, 접근 권한이 차단되기 전까지 누적 비용이 100만달러에 달한 사례도 확인됐다. AI 모델의 사용량에 따라 요금이 부과되는 클라우드 환경에서 자격 증명 탈취가 직접적인 대규모 금전 피해로 이어질 수 있다는 경고다.

구글 클라우드의 사이버 보안 전문기업 맨디언트(Mandiant)와 구글 위협 인텔리전스 그룹(GTIG)은 최근 'LLM재킹(LLMJacking)' 공격의 구체적인 작동 방식과 수익화 구조, 실제 피해 사례를 분석한 보고서를 3일(현지시간) 공개했다.

LLM재킹은 공격자가 기업의 대형언어모델(LLM) 접근 권한을 무단으로 확보한 뒤 고성능 AI 모델을 사용하거나, 해당 접근 권한을 제3자에게 판매하는 공격 수법이다. 기존의 크립토재킹(CryptoJacking)이 타인의 컴퓨팅 자원을 암호화폐 채굴에 이용하는 방식이라면, LLM재킹은 사용량에 따라 비용이 청구되는 AI 모델의 특성을 악용한다는 점에서 차이가 있다.

공격자가 탈취한 자격 증명으로 프런티어 AI 모델을 대량 호출하면 사용 요금은 정상적인 계정 소유자에게 부과된다. AI 모델의 성능이 높고 호출량이 많을수록 짧은 시간에 막대한 비용이 발생할 수 있다.

맨디언트와 구글 위협 인텔리전스 그룹이 분석한 최근 공격은 북미와 남미, 아시아·태평양 지역의 금융 서비스, 유통, 기술, 운송 기업 등 다양한 산업을 대상으로 발생했다. 공격자들은 자격 증명 탈취와 세션 하이재킹(Session Hijacking) 등을 통해 기업의 클라우드 환경에 침투했다. 공개된 깃허브(GitHub)에서 유효한 API 키나 계정 정보를 수집해 악용하는 사례도 확인됐다.

이처럼 확보한 접근 권한은 공격자가 직접 사용하는 데 그치지 않고 불법 AI 서비스 시장에서 거래되는 자산으로 활용되고 있다. 공격 수익화의 핵심에는 'LLM 믹서(LLM Mixers)'로 불리는 불법 중계 서비스가 있다. LLM 믹서는 여러 기업에서 탈취한 API 키와 모델 접근 권한을 하나의 중계 시스템으로 묶고, 이를 외부 이용자에게 저렴한 가격으로 판매하는 방식으로 운영된다.

공격자는 직접 AI 모델을 개발하거나 고가의 컴퓨팅 인프라를 구축하지 않고도 프런티어 모델에 대한 접근 권한을 상품처럼 판매할 수 있다. 실제 모델 사용 비용은 탈취당한 기업의 클라우드 계정에 청구된다.

구글 위협 인텔리전스 그룹은 이러한 불법 시장에서 기업 시스템에 처음 침입하는 공격자와 탈취한 자원을 판매하는 운영자가 역할을 나누는 분업 구조까지 확인했다고 밝혔다.

대표적인 사례가 불법 토큰 중계 서비스 '제트 나이트(Jet Night)'다. 이 서비스는 프런티어 AI 모델에 접근할 수 있다고 주장하며 월 약 60달러에 무제한 토큰 이용 상품을 판매했다.

구글에 따르면 해당 서비스의 운영에 이용된 탈취 계정에서는 8시간도 되지 않는 시간 동안 50만건 이상의 LLM API 호출이 발생했다. 이 과정에서 약 100만달러의 토큰 사용 비용이 피해 기업에 전가됐다.

공격자는 API 호출 한도를 우회하기 위해 단기간만 사용하는 서비스 계정을 반복적으로 생성하고 삭제하는 '소각 및 교체(Burn and Rotate)' 전략도 활용했다. 동시에 클라우드 서비스 제공업체의 청구 내역을 확인하면서 사용량과 비용 발생 상황을 감시했다.

또 다른 공격 사례에서는 기업의 클라우드 서비스 계정에 침입한 공격자가 추가 API 키를 생성하고 새로운 AI 서비스를 활성화해 단기간에 10만달러 이상의 사용 요금을 발생시켰다.

공격자들은 탈취한 자격 증명을 검증하는 과정에서도 탐지를 피하기 위한 수법을 사용했다. 공개된 코드 저장소에서 수집한 API 키가 실제로 작동하는지 확인할 때 단일 토큰만 생성하도록 요청하는 방식으로 비정상적인 대량 호출 탐지를 회피했다.

일부 공격자는 클라우드 환경에 침입한 뒤 내부 코드 저장소와 데이터베이스를 탐색해 추가 자격 증명을 확보하고, 관리자 권한을 획득하거나 새로운 서비스 계정을 생성해 접근을 유지했다.

구글은 AI 모델 중계 소프트웨어의 취약점도 새로운 공격 경로로 지목했다. 실제 조사에서는 라이트LLM(LiteLLM) 게이트웨이의 취약점인 CVE-2026-40217을 악용해 일반적인 가상 API 키의 권한을 관리자 수준으로 높인 사례가 확인됐다.

이처럼 LLM재킹은 단순히 API 키 하나를 탈취하는 수준을 넘어 클라우드 계정 침해, 권한 상승, AI 서비스 활성화, 대량 모델 호출, 불법 중계 서비스 운영으로 이어지는 복합적인 공격으로 발전하고 있다.

구글은 기업들이 AI 모델의 사용량과 비용을 지속적으로 감시하는 동시에 접근 권한을 최소화해야 한다고 강조했다. 특히 개발 환경과 운영 환경의 API 키를 분리하고, 개별 키가 호출할 수 있는 모델과 사용량을 제한할 것을 권고했다. 저비용 모델에 사용하도록 발급한 키가 고가의 프런티어 모델까지 호출하지 못하도록 권한을 세분화해야 한다는 것이다.

공개 코드 저장소에 포함된 자격 증명을 자동으로 탐지하는 시크릿 스캐닝(Secret Scanning)과 다중 인증(Multi-Factor Authentication, MFA), 클라우드 설정 점검도 주요 대응 방안으로 제시했다.

아울러 기업 내부에서 승인받지 않고 사용하는 AI 모델이나 도구를 의미하는 '섀도 LLM(Shadow LLM)'을 파악하고, 비정상적인 API 호출 증가와 새로운 AI 서비스 활성화, 예산 초과 징후 등을 조기에 탐지하는 체계가 필요하다고 설명했다.

구글은 모델별 API 호출 한도와 지출 예산을 설정하고, 비정상적인 사용량이 발생하면 신속하게 대응할 수 있도록 경고 체계를 구축할 것도 권고했다. 구글 위협 인텔리전스 그룹의 수석 애널리스트 존 헐트퀴스트(John Hultquist)는 공격자들이 LLM재킹을 활용해 공격 규모를 확대하고 있으며, 기업이 AI 자원에 대한 접근을 엄격히 통제해야 비용 피해와 추가적인 악용을 막을 수 있다고 강조했다.

그는 기업이 빠르게 도입하는 AI 모델과 컴퓨팅 자원을 면밀하게 감시하지 않으면 제3자가 이를 무단으로 이용할 수 있다며, 자원 사용 내역 점검과 다중 인증, 계정 정보 관리의 중요성을 지적했다.
articles.summary: 맨디언트와 구글 위협 인텔리전스 그룹이 탈취한 API 키·클라우드 계정으로 AI를 무단 호출하고 접근 권한을 재판매하는 LLM재킹 사례를 분석했다고 국내 매체가 보도했다. 기사에 따르면 불법 중계 서비스에 이용된 계정에서는 8시간 미만에 50만 건 이상의 호출이 발생해 피해 기업에 약 100만 달러의 비용이 전가됐다. 공격자들은 여러 기업의 접근 권한을 묶어 판매하고 서비스 계정을 반복 생성·삭제하는 방식도 활용했다. 사용량 기반 AI 서비스에서는 자격 증명 유출이 데이터 보안 문제뿐 아니라 즉각적인 대규모 비용 피해로 이어진다는 점을 보여준다.

articles.title: OpenAI Introduces Pando: A Git Backend That Cuts Median Push Latency ~80%
articles.content: OpenAI has introduced Pando, a new Git backend that now serves all development in its monorepo. The OpenAI Pando Git backend keeps the standard Git client and protocol. Engineers and Codex agents still run git push and git fetch as before. Only the server changed. OpenAI team reports median push latency fell nearly 80%. Pando now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. TL;DR Scale: Nearly 1 PB of Git data per day; peak above 57 TB in 1 hour. Runs on: Commodity hardware; standard cloud VMs saturate 10 Gbps links on clone and fetch. Performance: Thousands of concurrent pushers without degradation, per OpenAI’s own testing. Best: Median push latency down nearly 80% (about 5x). Worst: Not open source; repeat branch pushes resend non-trunk history (p99 pack under 3 MiB). What is OpenAI Pando? Pando is a Git-compatible server backend from OpenAI that scales concurrent pushes and fetches for a monorepo. It was written in Rust and reached production in 10 weeks. One engineer designed the core and teams of Codex agents implemented it. It has served production traffic since April 2026. Why did OpenAI need a new Git backend? Codex multiplied parallel work. OpenAI’s commit chart shows commits landed on master up 1,378% in Q3 2026 versus Q1 2024. Its Q4 2026 estimate is +2,442%. Each push now triggers many CI fetches. By late 2025, fetches and pushes slowed, merges failed, and reliability at times fell below 90%. OpenAI concluded the bottleneck was how it served Git, not Git itself. How does Pando work? Pando drops 2 assumptions that most Git servers treat as requirements: 1. Repository-wide consistency: Conventional servers order every ref update repo-wide, so unrelated pushes wait. Pando uses causal consistency instead. Each branch is serialized on its own, and clients only conflict when pushing the same ref. The tradeoff: a reader viewing several branches may see them at different points in time. 2. A unique packfile per client: Standard servers build a fresh pack per fetch. Pando stores each pushed pack as an immutable blob. A “ref version” goes into a scalable metadata store. A push needs O(1) metadata reads and writes. A fetch needs O(log Δ) reads, where Δ is the ref-version gap to close. How are pushes kept small and reusable? With millions of branches, a full ref advertisement can exceed 100 MiB. Pando advertises only the trunk branch as the base for new feature-branch pushes. Any reader with trunk history can then fetch that branch from 1 stored pack. In OpenAI’s monorepo, the median pack was under 20 KiB. How are fetches served at line rate? Pando returns download links via packfile-uri, an existing Git protocol feature. It sends an empty inline pack. A delivery service called Express caches packs regionally, using consistent hashing, with hit rates above 99%. What replaces garbage collection? Each push creates an “L0” pack. Background workers group packs into geometrically larger covers, similar to LSM-tree compaction. The monorepo currently uses covers up to L4. Covers act as a skip list, so pack selection runs in logarithmic time. & --> What are the production numbers? All figures below are self-reported by OpenAI. Median push latency reduced by nearly 80%. Nearly 1 PB of Git data per day, using only a handful of CPU cores. Over 57 TB of packs served in a single hour, more than 99% from local disk cache. Clones and fetches saturate 10 Gbps links on standard cloud VMs. OpenAI also ran a 1,000-writer simulation against 3-phase-commit and write-ahead-log designs. It labels these teaching models, not benchmarks. How does Pando compare with other approaches? OpenAI PandoGitHub SpokesAnthropic ScionGit client compatibleYes Yes No, own scn client Write coordinationPer-branch, causal consistencyThree-phase commit with quorumServer-side commits; refs via compare-and-swapDefault replicasNot disclosed (blob + metadata stores)5 full copies No fully materialized repo copyRead pathReused packs via packfile-uri, Express cacheClosest in-sync replicaTiered tree/blob cachesCache hit rateOver 99%Not disclosedOver 99% per tierHeadline resultMedian push latency down ~80%Serves ~1 billion repositories200x smaller CPU/memory footprintBuild effort10 weeks, RustNot disclosed7 people, 5 monthsAvailable to othersNoYes, powers GitHubNo How was Pando built and deployed? OpenAI wrote a Git conformance suite for agents and added deterministic simulation testing. Agents using GPT-6 Astra wrote Lean and TLA+ specs to find bugs. Pando first ran as a read- and write-through proxy, so traffic moved without downtime. OpenAI ships its own Git build to developer machines and the ChatGPT desktop app. What goes back to upstream Git? OpenAI fixed client handling of concurrent, interrupted and resumed pack downloads, and added packfile-uri tracing. Its build adds parallel pack indexing and “explicit haves.” Several fixes are upstream. The rest sit in a public patch tracker. What are the limitations? Pando is not open source; OpenAI team states that it is exploring ways to share the technology. Cross-branch reads have no single point-in-time snapshot. Repeat or stacked branch pushes resend everything outside trunk. The p99 pack was under 3 MiB. Every performance number is self-reported, with no independent benchmark yet. Key Takeaways Pando keeps Git, but rebuilds the server for parallel agent traffic. Per-branch causal consistency removes repository-wide write contention. Stored, reusable packs replace per-client pack generation. Median push latency dropped nearly 80%; daily traffic nears 1 PB. Client fixes go upstream; the backend stays internal for now. Check out the full OpenAI engineering post, the OpenAI Git repository and the patch tracker. articles.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
articles.content: Despite recent advances in CUAs, their development remains constrained by the limited diversity, controllability, and reliability of interaction data. Moreover, conventional optimization pipelines lack iterative feedback, while existing recursive improvement approaches often rely on self-generated experiences, limiting ability expansion and yielding diminishing returns. To address these challenges, we introduce CUA-Master, a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework. At the system level, an outer world-data-model flywheel continuously incorporates open-world corpus and leverages evolving model weaknesses to guide subsequent data construction and optimization iterations. At the data level, an inner flywheel couples open-world seeding and autocatalytic propagation. The former mines authentic workflows as seed tasks from instructional videos, and employs visual-semantic dual-path trajectory reconstruction; The latter transforms these seeds into reusable primitives for controllable synthesis of diverse, complex, and verifiable tasks. To enable efficient and reliable trajectory collection, we further introduce a feedback-guided snapshot-rollback retry mechanism in various real environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CUA-Master-27B achieves competitive performance across GUI-only and GUI-CLI hybrid benchmarks, scoring 80.2 on OSWorld Verified, 36.9 on OSWorld 2.0, 43.9 on WeaveBench, and 25.0 on Agents' Last Exam. Our framework also substantially improves the quality and efficiency of data synthesis, and exhibits continuous gains across recursive iterations.
articles.summary: CUA-Master는 실제 사용법 영상에서 작업을 추출하고 모델의 약점을 다음 데이터 생성에 반영하는 이중 반복 구조의 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트 학습 프레임워크다. 영상에서 복원한 작업을 재사용 가능한 요소로 분해해 검증 가능한 과제를 합성하며, 실제 환경에서는 스냅샷 복구와 재시도로 궤적 수집을 개선한다. 연구진은 27B 모델로 OSWorld Verified 80.2점, OSWorld 2.0 36.9점 등을 보고했다. 자체 생성 경험에만 의존하지 않고 외부 작업을 지속적으로 흡수하는 방식이 GUI 에이전트의 데이터 다양성과 학습 확장성을 높일 가능성을 제시한다.

articles.title: MEMENTO: Learning Context Management for Long Context Processing Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents that operate over long inputs must perform context management: deciding what to retain in a fixed-size context window. A common approach is compaction, where the model replaces its history with a self-generated note. Yet off-the-shelf agentic models, including GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.3, often write ineffective notes, and reinforcement learning (RL) alone rarely discovers useful note-taking behavior. We present MEMENTO, a long-context agent built on Qwen3-8B and trained to manage its context through compaction. We first bootstrap note-taking by fine-tuning on synthetic trajectories annotated with notes generated in hindsight, then reinforce it with RL using a reward that combines answer correctness, note-quality heuristics, and confidence calibration. Although trained only to compact into a fresh window, MEMENTO extends at test time to strategies such as context folding and confidence-based backtracking. On book-level question answering across four benchmarks, with books of up to 2.5M tokens, MEMENTO raises Qwen3-8B's accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8% while never holding more than 20K tokens in context. It outperforms GPT-5.5 agent in the same harness (13.1%) and full book context (56.7%) at less than 1/50 the cost. It also nearly matches a ~100x larger GLM-5.3 agent (69.3%) at 1/9 the cost, and comes within 6.4 points of GLM-5.3 full context at 1/26 the cost.
articles.summary: MEMENTO는 긴 입력을 처리할 때 어떤 정보를 메모로 남길지 학습하는 Qwen3-8B 기반 에이전트다. 사후 생성 메모를 포함한 합성 궤적으로 미세조정한 뒤 정답률·메모 품질·확신도 보정을 함께 보상하는 강화학습을 적용했다. 최대 250만 토큰 분량의 책을 다룬 네 가지 평가에서 컨텍스트를 2만 토큰 이하로 유지하며 정확도를 36.9%에서 67.8%로 높였다고 보고했다. 해당 실험에서는 GPT-5.5 기반 에이전트보다 높은 정확도와 50분의 1 미만 비용을 보여, 단순한 컨텍스트 확장 외에 학습된 정보 압축이 유효할 가능성을 제시한다.

articles.title: MXCode: Vector Quantization for MX-Native Inference at Scale
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00403v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory capacity and bandwidth are major bottlenecks in LLM inference, motivating weight compression beyond conventional 4-bit quantization. Vector quantization (VQ) enables approximately 2-bit weight storage but often relies on codebooks incompatible with native FP4 computation. We introduce MXCode (MX-Native Codebook Quantization), a framework bridging ultra-low-bit VQ compression with MicroXcaling (MX)-native FP4 computation. MXCode proposes three strategies: PostScale, which quantizes learned codebooks to MXFP4; PreScale, which extracts MX scales before codebook learning; and PreScale+, which further compresses these scales using VQ. These strategies explore tradeoffs among quantization quality, scale overhead, and codebook granularity. All reconstruct MX-native W4A4 operands without materializing intermediate high-precision weights. We evaluate MXCode on Qwen3 (235B), DeepSeek-R1 (671B), and GLM-5.2 (753B) using the Microsoft MX Emulation Library. MXCode achieves approximately 2 bits per weight with competitive, workload-dependent model quality. On GB300 hardware, experiments with Qwen3 (235B) show approximately 50% lower model-load memory than Native FP4 while maintaining near-Native-FP4 serving throughput. Under memory-constrained prefix reuse, P90 TTFT improves by up to 94.5%. These results demonstrate software-based reconstruction on existing FP4 hardware and inform the development of future MX-native inference systems.
articles.summary: MXCode는 약 2비트 벡터 양자화 저장과 MX 기반 FP4 연산을 연결하는 대형 모델 추론 프레임워크다. 코드북과 스케일을 처리하는 세 가지 전략으로 고정밀 중간 가중치를 만들지 않고 W4A4 연산 입력을 복원한다. GB300에서 Qwen3 235B를 평가한 결과 네이티브 FP4 대비 모델 적재 메모리를 약 50% 줄이면서 유사한 서빙 처리량을 유지했다고 보고했다. 메모리가 제한된 접두사 재사용 조건에서는 P90 첫 토큰 지연시간이 최대 94.5% 개선됐지만, 모델 품질과 이득은 작업 조건에 따라 달랐다.

articles.title: A generative foundation model for computational brain imaging
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00265v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational brain imaging is constrained by a mismatch between increasingly diverse tasks and scarce, heterogeneous clinical data. Although existing brain foundation models transfer pretrained representations, their knowledge remains entangled within model-specific features and fixed architectures. This paper proposes BrainGFM, a generative foundation model that extends knowledge transfer beyond representation reuse through a reusable and reconfigurable brain-imaging prior. By pretraining on a corpus of about 1.3 million MRI and CT slices, BrainGFM supported task-aligned data synthesis for low-data predictive learning and task-adapted post-training for image reconstruction. Across 48 downstream tasks, BrainGFM improved segmentation and classification under limited supervision and achieved high-fidelity image enhancement across heterogeneous imaging conditions. Multicenter clinical validation involving 4,796 stroke patients across two internal and four external centers demonstrated its applicability to three clinically relevant tasks around stroke cohorts. Blinded reader assessments showed that BrainGFM-generated FLAIR images approached acquired FLAIR in overall diagnostic quality. In a human-AI collaboration study, BrainGFM assistance yielded a 14% relative improvement in mean radiologist stroke-subtyping accuracy. These findings support generative priors as a reusable foundation for heterogeneous computational brain-imaging applications.
articles.summary: BrainGFM은 약 130만 장의 MRI·CT 단면 영상으로 사전학습한 생성형 뇌 영상 기반 모델이다. 재구성 가능한 영상 사전지식을 활용해 저데이터 예측용 합성 데이터와 영상 복원 작업을 지원하며, 48개 후속 과제에서 평가됐다. 6개 기관의 뇌졸중 환자 4,796명을 포함한 검증에서 합성 FLAIR 영상의 전반적 진단 품질이 실제 촬영 영상에 근접했고, 협업 실험에서는 영상의학과 의사의 뇌졸중 아형 분류 정확도가 평균적으로 상대 14% 개선됐다고 보고했다. 임상 활용 가능성을 뒷받침하지만, 이 결과만으로 모든 진단 상황에서 실제 촬영을 대체할 수 있다고 해석해서는 안 된다.

articles.title: Soniox STT v6 Adds Agent Text Input and Echo Filtering for Voice Agents
articles.content: Soniox has released Soniox STT v6, the latest generation of its speech-to-text API. Soniox STT v6 is a speech-to-text model that reads what a voice agent says while hearing the caller. It uses that text to recognize short replies and to drop the agent’s own voice. The release ships as stt-rt-v6 for streaming and stt-async-v6 for files, across 60+ languages. TL;DR Size: Soniox STT v6 is a proprietary hosted model, no parameter count published. Runs on: Soniox cloud API only (WebSocket streaming and async REST). No self-hosted or on-device option disclosed. Performance: Soniox calls it “significantly” more accurate than v5, but publishes no v6 numbers yet. Best: Price. $0.12/hour streaming and $0.10/hour async, with diarization and language ID bundled. Worst: Zero independent v6 results. Its v5 predecessor scored 1.34% semantic WER on Pipecat, behind v4’s 1.25%. What problem does Soniox STT v6 solve? In a cascaded voice agent, STT usually hears only the caller. It never sees the question being answered. Short answers suffer most. In Soniox’s docs, “River Roast” becomes “River Road” and “a tow” becomes “a tour.” The second problem is echo. Agent audio leaks back through speakerphones and laptops, gets transcribed as user speech, and the agent interrupts itself. How does agent text input work? You enable it with one flag in the start request: "enable_agent_text_input": true. It is only available on stt-rt-v6, not the async model. While the agent speaks, you stream its words on the same WebSocket as the caller’s audio. Each message is a small JSON frame: {"type": "agent_text", "text": "...", "end_of_segment": true}. Timing matters. Messages carry no timestamps, so the model places text where it arrives in the audio stream. Soniox recommends sending each piece 500 ms to 1 second before playback, paced by TTS timestamps. On barge-in, you flush what was already played, send end_of_segment: true, and drop the unplayed rest. The agent’s text never appears in the returned transcript. How does agent voice echo cancellation work? With agent text input on, v6 knows what the agent is saying. It uses that to separate leftover agent audio from caller speech and filter it out. It keeps listening during playback, so callers can still interrupt. It does not replace acoustic echo cancellation. It handles what your existing AEC leaves behind, so keep AEC on. What else changed in v6? Better voice typing: numbers, currencies, units, dates, IDs, names and specialized terms. Spoken commands like “period” or “new line” are written as words, so your app applies them. Improved meeting transcription and speaker diarization, live or recorded. Stronger accents, code-switching and language switching within a sentence. There is one formatting change to test before upgrading. v6 writes “15 dollars and 20 cents” as spoken, not “$15.20”. Hyphens in codes appear only when spoken. && How does Soniox compare on benchmarks? Soniox has not published v6 accuracy or latency numbers. Its benchmarks page still reports v5 on the open-source Pipecat STT benchmark. It uses 1,000 real-world samples and measures semantic WER plus time to final segment (TTFS). On it, stt-rt-v5 scores 1.34% semantic WER, 83.3% perfect transcripts and 260 ms median TTFS. Its P95 latency is 305 ms. Azure posts the lowest WER mean at 1.21%, but at 1,016 ms median latency. Soniox numbers are for v5, since v6 has not been benchmarked yet. Is Soniox really the first? Soniox calls v6 the first model that knows what your voice agent is saying. That claim needs a qualifier. AssemblyAI shipped agent context in Universal-3.5 Pro Realtime in July 2026. It also feeds the agent’s replies into streaming STT. The clearer difference is echo. Soniox’s docs describe filtering leaked agent audio using that text. AssemblyAI’s context docs describe no such filtering. Deployment, pricing and migration v6 is a drop-in swap: change the model name to stt-rt-v6 or stt-async-v6. The v5 models are deprecated and will be removed on December 15, 2026. After that, v5 requests route to v6 automatically. Pricing is token-based. Soniox lists about $0.12/hour streaming and $0.10/hour async. Agent text is billed as input text tokens, at $4.00 per 1M on real-time. Key Takeaways Soniox STT v6 reads the agent’s text to transcribe caller replies. Echo filtering removes leaked agent voice, on top of normal AEC. Streaming costs $0.12/hour, with diarization included. No v6 benchmark numbers exist yet; v5 scored 1.34% on Pipecat. v5 models retire December 15, 2026, with automatic routing to v6. Check out the Soniox STT v6 announcement, the agent text input docs and the v6 changelog. articles.title: 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기
articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기 NAVER D2 | 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기 naver.me ​ 발표 내용 다양한 관심사 추천 모델인 Multi-interest를 여러 지면에 적용하며 겪었던 문제를 해결했던 과정을 공유합니다. ​ 주제: Multi-interest 추천 모델(MINER)의 KREAM 실서비스 적용 사례 문제: 인기 상품 목록에서 특정 상품이 전체 유저에게 동시 노출되는 hubness 발생 분석: 점수를 유저 의존 성분과 유저 무관 성분으로 분해, 가설 3개를 실측으로 검증 조치: 유저 무관 성분 제거(centering, bias 분리), 추천 결과 다양화, 분포 지표 기반 평가 체계 도입 결과: 과노출 상품 전량 제거, 노출 상품 종류 +25%, 구매 지표 유지 시사점: 논문 구조의 실서비스 적용 시 발생하는 문제와 사전 점검 항목 ​ 발표 대상 Multi-interest 추천 모델에 관심 있으신 분들 ​ 목차 문제상황 가설 수립, 유저 의존 성분 + 유저 무관 성분 전략 1. 유저 무관 성분 낮추기 전략 2. 유저 유관 성분 높이기 전략 3. 두 성분을 지표에서 모니터링 남은 과제 및 점검항목 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.
articles.summary: 네이버가 다중 관심사 추천 모델 MINER를 KREAM에 적용하면서 특정 상품이 전체 사용자에게 집중 노출되는 허브니스 문제를 해결한 사례를 공개했다. 추천 점수를 사용자 의존 성분과 사용자 무관 성분으로 분해하고, 센터링·편향 분리 및 분포 지표 기반 평가를 도입했다. 발표에 따르면 과노출 상품을 모두 제거하고 노출 상품 종류를 25% 늘리면서 구매 지표는 유지했다. 논문 모델의 정확도만으로는 포착하기 어려운 실서비스 추천 편중을 분석하고 교정하는 구체적인 운영 사례다.

articles.title: TileWeave: Heterogeneous Tiling for Sparse Prefill on Mobile SoCs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Smartphone applications increasingly require large language models to process long contexts, whereas high prefill latency and memory demands constrain local inference. Block-sparse attention reduces computation and memory traffic, but its irregular selections conflict with mobile NPUs' preference for large, regular tiles. Efficient execution must exploit cross-query reuse while avoiding redundant computation and preserving selections needed for accuracy. In this paper, we present TileWeave, which partitions sparse attention by this cross-query reuse: highly shared key blocks run in coarse NPU tiles, while low-reuse blocks run on the GPU only for the query blocks that selected them. In addition, we design an NPU-native pooled-key selector that keeps selection inexpensive, and a runtime that publishes GPU partials in the order the NPU consumes them and merges them in its existing output store. On RULER, HeteroSparse matches XAttention's accuracy with Qwen3-1.7B and improves it with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; its mean LongBench scores match XAttention as well. On Snapdragon SM8750 and SM8850 phones, it achieves 1.35--3.23$\times$ faster full-model prefill than XAttention over 1k--16k tokens and up to 1.58$\times$ faster than dense attention.
articles.summary: TileWeave는 모바일 SoC에서 희소 어텐션의 키 블록 재사용 정도에 따라 NPU와 GPU에 작업을 나누는 긴 컨텍스트 추론 기법이다. 여러 쿼리가 공유하는 블록은 NPU의 큰 타일로 처리하고 재사용이 낮은 블록은 GPU에서 필요한 쿼리에 대해서만 계산한다. Snapdragon SM8750·SM8850 스마트폰의 1천~1만6천 토큰 조건에서 XAttention 대비 전체 모델 프리필을 1.35~3.23배 가속했다고 보고했다. 평가된 언어 모델에서 정확도를 유지하거나 개선해, 온디바이스 AI의 긴 입력 처리 지연을 줄일 가능성을 보여준다.

articles.title: Fidelity Collapses with Table Size, Not Turn Count: Delivery Architecture in a Deployed Tool-Using Agent
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00442v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When a multi-turn agent delivers a tool's structured records into the model's context and re-emits them each turn, every turn can corrupt data the tool computed correctly. We measure this in a production award-travel agent: two architectures over identical frozen payloads, lineage-matched prompts and sampling, differing only in delivery architecture. SYNTHESIS feeds full record sets into the planner's context and answers follow-ups in-head; BYPASS, the deployed system, keeps records in session state, translates follow-ups into arguments for a deterministic filter, and delivers rows over a typed side channel. Across 24 dialogues (339 scored turns per condition), BYPASS scores 92.3% of turns fully correct, SYNTHESIS 45.7% (paired gap +46.6pp [+35.7, +57.1]). Varying delivered-table size by capture date, SYNTHESIS collapses from near-perfect at 10 rows or fewer to 8% or less beyond about 74 rows. On a content-controlled prefix ladder the collapse threshold orders by model capability, from under 10 rows (GPT-4o-mini) to about 198 or more (Gemini 2.5 Pro), while BYPASS stays size-flat for all four models. The collapse is expensive: beyond 100 rows, where almost no SYNTHESIS answer is correct, each correct one costs roughly 200x BYPASS's flat \$0.012. Practitioners converged on typed side-channel delivery for rendering, not correctness; we show it was, unknowingly, also a correctness decision.
articles.summary: 실서비스 항공 보상 여행 에이전트를 분석한 연구가 도구의 구조화된 데이터를 LLM이 다시 출력하게 하는 방식과 별도의 타입 지정 채널로 전달하는 방식을 비교했다. 세션 상태에 기록을 보관하고 결정적 필터로 후속 요청을 처리한 BYPASS는 24개 대화에서 턴 단위 완전 정답률 92.3%를 기록해, 전체 기록을 모델 컨텍스트에 넣는 SYNTHESIS의 45.7%를 크게 웃돌았다. SYNTHESIS의 오류는 대화 횟수보다 표 크기에 민감했으며, 관측된 일부 조건에서는 약 74행을 넘자 정답률이 8% 이하로 떨어졌다. 정확한 도구 결과를 모델이 재서술하지 않도록 전달 구조를 설계하는 것이 신뢰성과 비용 모두에 중요함을 보여주는 제한된 실서비스 사례다.

articles.title: Decentralized Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication in Shared Codebases
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00314v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents working in shared repositories may receive separate, independently-motivated requests from human developers, creating a setting that is multi-agent by necessity. When this scenario happens, their individual implementations may work separately but conflict when combined. To study this setting, we introduce ParallACT, a benchmark of orchestrator-free multi-agent coding tasks. ParallACT contains both complementary and contradictory tasks. In complementary tasks, each agent's task is separately useful and implementations must share an interface to be productively combined. In contradictory pairs, both agents' tasks require editing the same code in incompatible ways, and naively combining independent solutions fails to produce a useful implementation. We compare a single-agent oracle given the combined set of tasks against multi-agent settings that vary execution order, visibility, awareness of other agents, and access to a communication channel. We find that the oracle solves most tasks while parallel agents perform substantially worse. Their performance drop is notable for complementary tasks, and particularly sharp for contradictory tasks (e.g., from 62% to 16% for Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.8) where merged code typically satisfies only one specification, and the same gap appears in all six further configurations pairing two agent harnesses with three open-weight models. Simply telling an agent that a peer exists does not help significantly, and giving agents access to a communication channel recovers only a small part of the performance, at an additional token cost. ParallACT thus identifies and isolates a core challenge that will become more common as multi-agent coding by independent principals becomes standard, and provides a controlled test of which coordination strategies help, and at what cost.
articles.summary: ParallACT는 중앙 조정자 없이 같은 저장소에서 서로 다른 요청을 수행하는 코딩 에이전트들의 협업을 평가하는 벤치마크다. 상호 보완적인 과제뿐 아니라 동일 코드를 양립 불가능하게 수정해야 하는 과제를 포함해, 개별 구현의 성공과 통합 결과의 성공을 구분한다. 상충 과제의 한 평가에서는 전체 요청을 받은 단일 에이전트의 성공률 62%가 병렬 에이전트 설정에서 16%로 하락했다. 다른 에이전트의 존재를 알리거나 통신 채널을 제공하는 것만으로는 충분히 회복되지 않아, 병렬 코딩 확대에 맞춘 명시적 조정 설계가 필요함을 시사한다.

articles.title: On the Limits of Test-Time Compute for Self-Evaluation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-verification and aggregation have emerged as popular approaches for bridging the gap between pass@1 and pass@N. However, increasing the number of candidates does not consistently narrow the gap between final-answer accuracy and pass@N. To understand this limitation, we use ranking error to measure how reliably models distinguish their correct generations from incorrect ones. We show that ranking error admits a bias-variance decomposition, with both components shaped by algorithmic design choices and inference compute. Across our experiments, additional compute reduces variance, while bias initially decreases before approaching a plateau. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Scorpio, a simple and general method that jointly scores randomly grouped candidates. Across math, code, and puzzle benchmarks, Scorpio improves verification, tree search, and aggregation. For verification, Scorpio improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 7 percentage points while matching or exceeding that baseline's peak accuracy with 17-42% lower inference cost. For tree search, using Scorpio to score partial solutions and select the final answer improves accuracy by up to 10 percentage points over prior methods. Finally, Scorpio improves the scaling of aggregation-based methods by 11 percentage points on coding tasks.
articles.summary: 추론 후보를 많이 생성해도 최종 정답 선택이 비례해 개선되지 않는 이유를 자기평가의 순위 오류로 분석한 연구다. 추가 연산은 분산을 줄이지만 편향 개선은 정체되는 경향을 관찰하고, 무작위로 묶은 후보들을 함께 채점하는 Scorpio를 제안했다. 수학·코드·퍼즐 평가에서 검증 정확도를 가장 강한 기준선보다 최대 7%포인트 높이고, 해당 기준선의 최고 정확도 이상을 17~42% 낮은 추론 비용으로 달성했다고 보고했다. 후보 생성량뿐 아니라 평가·선택 방식이 테스트 시점 연산의 효율을 좌우한다는 결과다.

articles.title: AStockArena: Beyond Returns, Can We Entrust Real Capital to the Decisions of Financial Agents?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00515v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in dynamic financial trading, yet real-time trading benchmarks mainly evaluate agents by cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance. Such outcome metrics cannot show whether trades are faithfully reported, supported by available evidence, and consistent with account states. We introduce AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for continuous trading in China's A-share market. Under shared market conditions and execution constraints, we evaluate 13 open- and closed-source models over 3,198 sequential decisions. AStockArena reconstructsthe actions actually posted to accounts by aligning reports, trade requests, execution responses, and account states, and audits them with eight checks spanning execution traceability (O), evidence sufficiency (RK), and financial meta-awareness (B), combining record verification with consensus expert annotation. Of 1,070 trading points, 72.99% exhibit at least one audit gap; model-level rates range from52.2% to 91.2%, with evidence gaps most prevalent. Historical trade-filtering replay further shows thatportfolio outcomes are sensitive to these flagged trades. Decision-process auditing thus offers a verifiable complement to return-based evaluation of financial agents.
articles.summary: AStockArena는 중국 A주 시장에서 금융 에이전트의 수익률뿐 아니라 보고 내용·주문·체결 응답·계좌 상태의 일치 여부를 감사하는 벤치마크다. 13개 모델의 연속 의사결정 3,198건을 대상으로 실행 추적성, 근거 충분성, 재무 상태 인식에 관한 여덟 가지 점검을 수행했다. 1,070개 거래 시점 중 72.99%에서 하나 이상의 감사 공백이 발견됐고, 근거 부족이 가장 흔했다. 이는 손실이나 부정 거래의 비율을 뜻하지는 않지만, 실자금 운용의 신뢰성을 수익 지표만으로 판단하기 어렵다는 점을 보여준다.

articles.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
articles.content: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.
articles.summary: EgoActionBench는 1인칭 사람 영상에서 행동의 내용·시점·사용한 손을 함께 평가하는 세밀한 행동 캡셔닝 벤치마크다. 1,407개 에피소드에 사람이 다듬은 행동 주석 41,132개를 포함하며, 의미 일치도와 시간적 겹침, 정밀도·재현율을 함께 측정한다. 지도 미세조정과 강화학습을 거친 두 모델은 EgoActionScore가 각각 15.9점과 23.2점 개선됐고 평가된 오픈소스 기준선을 모두 앞섰다. 사람 영상을 로봇 학습에 활용하려면 일반적인 영상 이해를 넘어 원자적 행동과 양손의 역할을 정확히 구분해야 함을 드러낸다.

articles.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
articles.content: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer.
articles.summary: TechCrunch에 따르면 AI 추론 스타트업 Fal이 Bessemer 주도로 13억 달러를 조달했다. 기업가치는 160억 달러로 두 배 상승했으며, 보도는 추론 수요 확대를 배경으로 제시했다. 대규모 자금이 모델 개발뿐 아니라 추론 서비스 사업에도 유입되고 있음을 보여주지만, 제공된 기록에는 매출·수익성이나 기술 성능을 평가할 세부 수치가 없다.

articles.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
articles.content: Apple's new App Store rules will require 18+ ratings for dating apps and AI companions that offer sexual or romantic content.
articles.summary: Apple이 새로운 App Store 규정에서 데이팅 앱과 성적·낭만적 콘텐츠를 제공하는 AI 동반자 앱에 18세 이상 등급을 요구한다고 보도됐다. 모든 AI 앱을 제한하는 조치가 아니라 관계형·성인 콘텐츠를 제공하는 특정 유형의 앱을 대상으로 한다. 해당 개발사에는 콘텐츠와 연령 등급 정책을 점검해야 하는 변화이며, 제공된 기록에는 구체적인 시행 일정이나 연령 확인 방식은 제시되지 않았다.
